phases.message: I'm Greta Valdivia, Marrowby Mills. First, at Certifield Organic, read the rules for our annual update and the changes already accepted this year. Don't put anything in the update yet: I'll send you to our papers, our purchasing system and the registry next.
These are our papers: last year's plan, our suppliers' certificates, our change memos and our import files. Read all of them.
This is our purchasing system. Read every supplier and every receipt this year, on both pages of each.
This is the organic registry. Look up every supplier of ours there, on both pages, and read every import certificate.

Back at Certifield Organic. Put into the annual update what it needs: each change to our plan, made or planned, each supplier of organic ingredients that is no longer certified, and the certificate number of each import that matches its shipment. Leave out what is not a change, what is outside our plan, what needs no certificate, and anything already accepted. Then tell me what you put in, and what you left out and why.

rules.text: Certifield Organic, the certifier's client portal. Friday 9 October 2026. Topics: update, plan, suppliers, imports, exempt. Marrowby Mills' annual update is due 30 November 2026.

Friday 9 October 2026. The annual update (7 CFR 205.406(a)) gives: a summary of the changes made to the organic system plan since last year's, with documents; the additions and deletions planned for the coming year; changes to the operation's information; and what else the certifier needs. A change reported during the year and accepted is already in the plan and is not reported again.

Friday 9 October 2026. The plan (205.201(a)) lists inputs and practices, and describes how the operation verifies its suppliers and the organic status of what it receives, to prevent fraud. A new ingredient, supplier, site or machine is a change to it. A purchase that was cancelled and a machine never installed are not changes.

Friday 9 October 2026. A supplier's organic status is read in the Organic Integrity Database, here the registry Organicheck, and not from its paper certificate, which can be older or newer than the status. Certified means current. Suspended, revoked, surrendered or expired means not certified. A supplier of organic ingredients that is no longer certified is reported in the update and taken off the approved list. A supplier of only a non-organic product is outside the plan.

Friday 9 October 2026. Each organic import needs an NOP Import Certificate issued in the Organic Integrity Database (205.273), and the importer verifies that its data match the shipment: the product and the quantity. Log the certificate number of each import that matches. A shipment that does not match is not logged as compliant. A domestic purchase, or an import of a non-organic product, needs no certificate.

Friday 9 October 2026. Some operations need no certification (205.101): for example, one that only receives, stores and prepares for shipment sealed, tamper-evident packages. Such a supplier has no certificate in the registry. It is not a lapsed one: its source and its records are verified instead.

docs.title: Organic system plan, accepted 14 November 2025
docs.text: Plan accepted 14 November 2025 for Marrowby Mills LLC, product Organic Granola. Approved organic suppliers: Verdane Oats Cooperative, Honeyfield Apiary, Sunmere Almond Growers, Pellwick Pantry Supply, Lowmoor Coconut Oil, Ceylonwell Spice, Cacaoreef Traders, Vallambra Vanilla. Premises: one warehouse, Dock A. Equipment: one oat roaster, one drying line. Suppliers are verified on receipt of their paper certificates.

docs.text: Paper certificate of organic operation, Verdane Oats Cooperative, issued 30 April 2024, valid to 30 April 2025. The cooperative has sent no newer paper copy.

docs.title: Certificate: Honeyfield Apiary
docs.text: Paper certificate of organic operation, Honeyfield Apiary, issued 30 June 2025, valid to 30 June 2026.

docs.title: Certificate: Sunmere Almond Growers
docs.text: Paper certificate of organic operation, Sunmere Almond Growers, issued 1 April 2025, valid to 31 March 2026.

docs.title: Statement: Pellwick Pantry Supply
docs.text: Statement from Pellwick Pantry Supply, 3 February 2026. Pellwick only buys, stores and ships sunflower seeds in sealed, tamper-evident 25 kg sacks packed and labelled organic by Ridgeback Seed Co.; it opens none and is exempt from certification under 7 CFR 205.101(e). It keeps records of every sack.

docs.title: Memo C-1: dried cranberries added
docs.text: Memo C-1, 1 June 2026, Greta Valdivia. Organic dried cranberries are now an ingredient in the Organic Granola, from Kestrel Dried Fruit, a new supplier. The first delivery came on 12 August 2026. This is not in the plan accepted in November 2025.

docs.title: Memo C-2: second warehouse
docs.text: Memo C-2, 1 July 2026, Greta Valdivia. Marrowby Mills leased a second warehouse, Dock B, and has stored organic ingredients there since 1 July 2026. The plan names only Dock A.

docs.title: Memo C-3: second oat roaster, planned
docs.text: Memo C-3, 22 September 2026, Greta Valdivia. A second oat roaster is to be installed on 9 March 2027. It is ordered and paid for; it is not yet installed.

docs.title: Memo C-5: pouch filler order cancelled
docs.text: Memo C-5, 12 May 2026, Greta Valdivia. The order for a new pouch filler was cancelled on 12 May 2026. It was never delivered or installed.
